title: [iOS] Add AccessKit screen reader support
body:
> [!NOTE]
> AI-assisted contribution disclosure:
Claude Code was used to help generate an initial boilerplate draft based on the existing macOS AccessKit implementation and to explore unfamiliar APIs. The generated code was not accepted as-is and required significant manual debugging, modification, integration work, and testing.
The implementation was built, exported, and tested manually on physical iOS hardware with VoiceOver enabled. Additional fixes and follow-up changes were made during review and integration.
This PR should be considered AI-assisted, not AI-authored.

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

iOS is currently the only major Godot platform without screen reader support. macOS, Windows, and Linux already integrate the AccessKit-based `AccessibilityServerAccessKit` driver, but iOS has no implementation, so VoiceOver cannot read `Control` elements or their `accessibility_name` / `description` / `role` properties in apps exported from Godot.

This PR adds the missing iOS glue so VoiceOver works out of the box, using the same driver and the upstream `accesskit_ios_subclassing_adapter`.

- Closes #

## Additional information

### What changed

- **`drivers/accesskit/accessibility_server_accesskit.{h,cpp}`** - Adds an `APPLE_EMBEDDED_ENABLED` branch alongside the existing macOS / Windows / Linux paths in `window_create` / `window_destroy` / `update_if_active`, using AccessKit's 3-callback iOS variant.
- **`platform/apple_embedded/display_server_apple_embedded.{h,mm}`** - Registers `godotView` as the host `UIView` with `AccessibilityServer::window_create`, advertises `FEATURE_ACCESSIBILITY_SCREEN_READER`, and surfaces VoiceOver state via `accessibility_screen_reader_active()` backed by `UIAccessibilityIsVoiceOverRunning`.
- **`platform/ios/detect.py`** - Adds an `accesskit_sdk_path` SCons option mirroring the macOS pattern, links the appropriate device / simulator static slice, and defines `ACCESSKIT_ENABLED` when found.
- **`drivers/SCsub`** - Includes the AccessKit driver sources in the iOS build.

### Scope decisions

- **visionOS deliberately not enabled.** The `APPLE_EMBEDDED_ENABLED` guard would cover it, but visionOS is kept out of `drivers/SCsub` and `platform/visionos/detect.py` to limit this PR's scope. Happy to follow up in a separate PR.
- **No new script-exposed API.** No `doc/classes/` changes are required - the feature surfaces through the existing `AccessibilityServer` API and `Control.accessibility_*` properties already documented for the other platforms.

### Dependency status

This PR depends on **AccessKit C 0.22.1** (released 2026-05-24, [AccessKit/accesskit-c#94](https://github.com/AccessKit/accesskit-c/pull/94)), which introduces the iOS adapters.

A matching **godot-accesskit-c-static** release with iOS binaries (`lib/ios/{arm64,simulator_arm64}/static/libaccesskit.a`) is still pending. Until that lands, the PR can be built by compiling `accesskit-c` 0.22.1 locally and pointing `accesskit_sdk_path=...` at the resulting tree. **Suggest holding merge until the static-bindings release is cut.**

### Test plan

Manual VoiceOver testing - no automated tests added. The change is platform glue with no host-testable surface, matching how the macOS / Windows / Linux AccessKit integrations were merged.

Tested with VoiceOver enabled on:
- [x] iOS device (arm64) - `Control` nodes are reachable via swipe navigation; `accessibility_name`, `description`, and `role` are announced
- [x] Confirmed no regression with VoiceOver disabled

Reviewers wanting to reproduce: build `accesskit-c` 0.22.1 with the iOS targets, then:

```bash
scons platform=ios target=template_debug arch=arm64 accesskit_sdk_path=/path/to/accesskit-c
```
